newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse turnover boosted by special lots.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse turnover boosted by special lots.

text.p: Trading on the three-day special board boosted turnover at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Friday, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 23.798 million shillings traded on 682,839 shares from 18.864 million shillings traded on 469,061 shares. The index lost 3.69 points to stand at 2,998.

Some 70,000 shares of Nation Printers & Publishers dealt at 109 from 107, 281,000 shares of National Bank of Kenya was unchanged at 14.50 and 100,000 shares of Rea Vipingo were traded at 10.50 from 10.65 on the three-day board.
Trading on the normal floor in the market was low.
On average, prices across the board declined marginally causing the index drop.
Uchumi Supermarket eased to 44.25 from 44.50, while Diamond Trust Bank lost 50 cents to close at 32.50. Bamburi Cement closed at 28 unchanged, while Kenya Breweries closed at 48.50 from 48.75.
In the agriculturals, Rea Vipingo remains the most actively traded share. It closed unchanged at 10.65.
"Since the foreign exchange position of the shares on the counter is the same, it remains a good place to hide. It is a fairly liquid share," a senior broker said.
Kenya Airways lost five cents to close at 8.90.
Foreigners remained active players in the market dominating the trading in Kenya Commercial Bank.

"There is a lot of complacency among our local investors. Part of the reason could be due to the disappointment of declining share prices, like Kenya Airways, which is now trading at 8.90 from an initial offer price of 11.50," one broker said.
"In the long term though, this is the best time to buy shares in the market. Prices are low," he added.
